reasons: The imageUrl input is accepted but never used.

terms.meaning: a reusable piece of screen that can be placed wherever it is needed.
the inputs a component is given when it is used.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup for the shared pieces
sections.what: Brings in the layout pieces, icons and theme values that all the small components share.
sections.why: Standard setup at the top of a shared file.

sections.name: ChipProps
sections.title: Inputs for the tag component
sections.what: Describes what a tag needs: a label, an optional icon, a color, a filled or outlined look, and a small or medium size.
sections.why: Makes the tag's inputs clear to anyone using it.
sections.watch_out: Only the label is required; everything else has a default.

sections.name: Chip
sections.title: Small colored tag
sections.what: Draws a small rounded tag with a label and optional icon. Filled tags have a faint tint of the color; outlined tags show only a thin border.
sections.why: Likely reason: a compact way to show a category or label.
sections.watch_out: The color is turned into a faint tint by adding digits to its end, so a color name or a three-digit hex code will produce an invalid color.

sections.name: StatusBadgeProps
sections.title: Inputs for the status badge
sections.what: Lists the status values a badge can show: normal, low, high, critical, info and pending.
sections.why: Limits badges to known statuses so their colors stay consistent.
sections.watch_out: A new status must be added here and in the color map below, or it will show in gray.

sections.name: StatusBadge
sections.title: Status badge
sections.what: Draws a small colored pill with a dot and a text label, such as Normal or High. The label defaults to the status word with a capital first letter.
sections.why: Lets health results be read at a glance through consistent colors.
sections.watch_out: An unknown status shows as gray rather than raising an error, so a typo can go unnoticed.

sections.name: AvatarProps
sections.title: Inputs for the avatar
sections.what: Describes what the round initials circle needs: a name, a size, an optional image address and an optional color.
sections.watch_out: The image address is accepted but never used, so passing a photo still shows initials.

sections.name: Avatar
sections.title: Round initials avatar
sections.what: Draws a round circle with the first letters of the name, for example Asha Rao shows AR. The circle and its letters scale together with the chosen size.
sections.why: Gives each person a recognizable mark when there is no photo.
sections.watch_out: Only the first two initials are shown, and an empty name gives an empty circle.

sections.name: SectionHeaderProps
sections.title: Inputs for the section heading
sections.what: Describes a heading with a title, an optional smaller subtitle and an optional action with a label and a press handler.
sections.watch_out: The action is a plain text link, which can be a small target to tap.

sections.name: SectionHeader
sections.title: Section heading
sections.what: Draws a section heading with an optional subtitle and an optional tappable link on the right.
sections.why: Likely reason: repeated headings look the same everywhere.
sections.watch_out: The link is plain text, so it may be hard to tap on small screens.

sections.name: Divider
sections.title: Thin divider line
sections.what: Draws a thin horizontal line between list items. Extra styling can be passed in to change its spacing.
sections.why: Likely reason: separates items in a list so they are easier to read.

sections.name: EmptyStateProps
sections.title: Inputs for the empty-state placeholder
sections.what: Describes the icon, title and subtitle needed for a placeholder shown when a list has nothing in it.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps placeholder messages consistent.

sections.name: EmptyState
sections.title: Empty-state placeholder
sections.what: Shows a centered message with a round icon, a heading and a short explanation. It also holds the shared styles for every component in this file.
sections.why: Gives the user a clear message instead of a blank screen.
sections.watch_out: The styles at the bottom are shared by all components here, so changing one style changes every component that uses it.

summary: Small reusable visual pieces: tags, status badges, initials avatars, section headings, dividers and empty-state placeholders.
purpose: Lets screens share the same small building blocks with the same look.
why: Likely reason: avoids repeating the same styling in many screens.
how: Each component takes a few inputs and draws a styled view. Shared styles are gathered at the bottom of the file.
inputs: Text labels, optional icons and colors, sizes, status values, names for avatars, and optional press actions on headings.
outputs: Drawn components on screen. Nothing is saved or fetched.
risks: Unknown status values show as a plain gray badge. The avatar ignores its image input. The heading link is small text that is hard to tap.
debug: If a component looks wrong, check the colors and sizes passed in, and that the status is one of the listed values. If initials look wrong, check the spacing in the name.
